venture.headline: Daniel Ek backs AI researcher’s fusion power startup. Here’s what they’re building.
venture.summary: Spotify founder Daniel Ek is backing Europa Fusion, a fusion power startup founded by an AI researcher. Here's what the startup is building.

venture.headline: Is selling an AI version of your face to this microdrama startup the future of Hollywood?
venture.summary: An actor has licensed his face to a microdrama startup — in a trend that's already popular in China. Experts question the long-term consequences if this becomes a trend in Hollywood, too.

research.headline: AgentRoboCritic Analyzes Frontier Agent Direct Robot Control
research.summary: Researchers introduce AgentRoboCritic, an intent-grounded critique framework providing action-level analysis of frontier multimodal language agents on direct robot control. The study evaluates agents across 12 manipulation benchmarks, highlighting capabilities like closed-loop recovery and limitations such as physical execution bottlenecks. Additionally, the project releases a dataset of 12,844 annotated actions and the Muse-Glimmer-30B fine-tuned open-source critic.

research.headline: The most misunderstood graph in AI just got a major update
research.summary: A new report from the AI evaluation nonprofit METR finds that some AI capabilities are continuing to improve along an exponential trajectory—but it also indicates that models aren’t quite as good at tasks that require judgment as they are at coding. The report is an update to the organization’s time horizon plot, which was widely….

research.headline: Building AI that can work across the enterprise
research.summary: For years, enterprises have approached AI as a series of discrete experiments. Now, as AI agents begin to move into the workflows that run the business, that model is starting to look inadequate. Organizations moving from isolated pilots toward AI agents and autonomous workflows are confronting a deeper challenge: rethinking how data, business processes, governance,….

research.headline: Active Feature Acquisition by Distilling an Oracle Teacher
research.summary: Acquiring every feature of an instance is often costly: a measurement can carry a monetary price, a time delay, or a privacy cost. Active Feature Acquisition (AFA) addresses this by learning a policy that decides, per instance, which features to acquire under a budget. Existing AFA methods train this policy by optimizing a self-constructed utility target rather than distilling an explicit teacher.

research.headline: PlayCraft: Designing Engaging Games from Agent Play Experience
research.summary: Recent AI agents can generate playable games, but these games are not necessarily engaging. Mastery is a key source of engagement, yet designing for it requires extensive human play and tuning. We propose PlayCraft, an automated framework that uses a vision-based agent to play games and draws on its detailed play experience to revise them for mastery.

titans.summary: Today, I’m talking with Hayden Field, The Verge’s senior AI reporter, about the Anthropic IPO for the third and final episode in our series about AI in real life. The AI lab behind Claude went public on the Nasdaq last Thursday. The numbers are gigantic, but not really that important for this conversation, except to […].

titans.headline: Anthropic mathematician claims to have solved prestigious Millennium Prize problem with Claude
titans.summary: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge claims he has proved the Riemann hypothesis, one of mathematics's most notoriously difficult problems, with the help of Claude, cracking a puzzle that has eluded some of the world's best mathematicians for decades. If verified, it would mark yet another seismic achievement for AI in mathematics and add to the upheaval […].

regulatory.headline: Ten Additional States Join FTC Lawsuit Against Dollar General
regulatory.summary: Ten states have joined the Federal Trade Commission's amended complaint as co-plaintiffs in a lawsuit against Dollar General Corporation. The suit alleges the company engaged in deceptive pricing practices by charging customers higher prices at the register than advertised on shelves.

regulatory.headline: FTC Takes Enforcement Action Against Harness Maker Over False USA Claims
regulatory.summary: The Federal Trade Commission has taken enforcement action against safety-harness manufacturer Elk River Inc. for allegedly making false 'Made in USA' claims. A proposed order requires the company to cease deceptive claims and pay a monetary judgment.

voices.headline: Bob Woodward Is Scared as Hell
voices.summary: In his new memoir, the legendary reporter asks why presidents keep starting dumb wars—and worries about the future.

frontier.headline: X-ray telescope captures first cosmic observations after eight years
frontier.summary: After traveling 10 billion kilometers in space over eight years, an X-ray telescope heading to Mercury has successfully captured its first cosmic observations. The instrument is performing better than expected and may soon reveal Mercury's chemical secrets and formation history.

frontier.headline: Time may be far stranger than we realize. Scientists have a way to test it
frontier.summary: Time may be far stranger than we realize, and scientists have proposed a way to detect clocks experiencing multiple flows of time simultaneously. Using atomic clocks with dramatically enhanced sensitivity, researchers hope to reveal a never-before-observed quantum effect that could transform our understanding of time and gravity.

frontier.headline: A giant star swallowed another star. James Webb reveals the aftermath
frontier.summary: Astronomers have witnessed a spectacular cosmic collision in the Andromeda galaxy, where a small star spiraled into a giant star 18,000 times brighter than the Sun, triggering a violent eruption. NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope captured the aftermath just 47 days later, revealing new details about how two stars can merge into one.

frontier.headline: Fast, in-place, and ancilla-free quantum algorithms for integer multiplication and inversion
frontier.summary: Arithmetic operations are a fundamental building block in the design of quantum algorithms, with their implementation cost expected to have a significant impact on the viability of a wide variety of quantum applications. In this work, we present novel algorithms for a number of in-place quantum arithmetic operations that are highly efficient in terms of their space and gate count overheads compared to the current state-of-the-art. We show that in-place modular multiplication of integers, modulo a power of two, can be performed with either a classical or quantum odd multiplier using $O(n^{1+ε})$ gates and no ancilla qubits, for any $ε>0$.

frontier.headline: Scalable Simulation of Strongly Correlated Fermions with Neural Gaussian Tensor Networks
frontier.summary: Accurate simulations of strongly correlated electrons remain a central challenge in computational physics. We introduce neural-network Gaussian projected entangled-pair states (NN-GPEPS), which exploit the locally-entangled subspace of Gaussian states to give an architecture more compatible with modern neural networks and an exact contraction cost of $O(N^{3/2})$ on two-dimensional lattices. For the Hubbard model at $U/t=8$ and $1/8$ hole doping, we obtain state-of-the-art variational energies in large lattices of up to 1024 sites.

industry.headline: The ‘GTA 6’ Work Blackout Is Here
industry.summary: From taking sick days and vacation days to gaming at the office, many are going all out to embrace the franchise’s long-awaited release.

voices.headline: Voters embrace 'no take, only throw' politics amidst rising cost of living
voices.summary: American voters are simultaneously demanding increased government spending and lower taxes, creating an unsustainable fiscal dynamic termed "no take, only throw" politics. Ongoing inflation, driven in part by massive federal budget deficits and various policy decisions, has severely strained household finances. While politicians from both parties promise relief without imposing costs on the middle class, failing to balance revenue and spending risks exacerbating inflation.

voices.headline: Reflecting on American Democracy and Trump's Failed Autocracy
voices.summary: An author reflects on previously warning that America was becoming an authoritarian state under Trump, noting that those fears underestimated Trump's incompetence as a dictator and overrated his ambitions. A free election delivered an overwhelming rebuke to Trump's rule, demonstrating the resilience of American democracy, the strength of decentralized state and local election systems, and the courts. Ultimately, ordinary Americans turned against Trump's corruption and callous excesses during a time of rising prices, proving that public commitment to a self-governing republic remains intact.

voices.headline: Hollywood Must Partner with New Technology and Creator Platforms to Evolve
voices.summary: Hollywood faces a cultural shift as audiences increasingly look to creator platforms like YouTube, Roblox, and TikTok rather than traditional studios. While AI accelerates this transition, moviemakers can adapt by collaborating with AI-backed and creator-focused studios, much like Disney once partnered with Pixar. Studios must move beyond treating creator platforms merely as farm systems and instead integrate audience input and new technologies into their storytelling process.

voices.headline: Republican gerrymandering still inflicted structural harm despite midterm failures
voices.summary: Analyses suggesting Republican gerrymandering failed entirely because Democrats won some races ignore the enduring structural harm of manipulated maps. Despite high voter turnout overcoming efforts to insulate incumbents, the maps successfully limited Democratic gains and protected partisan advantages. Experts emphasize that the difficulty of overcoming these maps does not render them legitimate or harmless.

voices.headline: Grand Theft Auto VI Blurs the Line Between Simulation and Life
voices.summary: The massive release of Grand Theft Auto VI immerses players in a detailed simulation of Florida called Leonida, echoing the menial routines and tracking metrics of real life. Playing as the character Jason, the author notes how in-game tasks like feeding a snake or drinking coffee mirror the quantified metrics and simulated rituals of modern daily existence. The boundary between virtual entertainment and real-world labor has dissolved into a continuous loop of digital management.
